correctness.rationale: Stationarity and the common positive multiplier give transition kernel P_{ij}=π_j+e^{−ΔΛ}(1_{i=j}−π_j). Expanding E∏(1−p_i X_i) over all eight hidden triples yields N(u)=C+A exp(−u)+B exp(−L+u), with A=π(1−π)p1p2(1−πp3)>0 and B=π(1−π)p2p3(1−πp1)>0. N is strictly convex and the free minimizer is (L+log A/B)/2; clipping is exact and Λ strictly increasing proves unique physical time. Conditional repeated attempts are independent even if visits coincide; with p2=0 uniqueness would fail and is explicitly excluded. Independent eight-path summation over four diverse parameter sets reproduces both interior and endpoint optima, but the universal theorem comes from algebra.

value.rationale: A closed-form globally optimal middle survey time is an actionable exact design benchmark for intermittent Markov availability with heterogeneous visits, including precise endpoint collapse and a surprising cancellation of the middle detectability. It is a small, clearly scoped optimization rather than a routine stationary-Markov identity.

final_claim: For a stationary common-clock binary continuous-time Markov availability process with independent conditional detection attempts of fixed p1,p2,p3>0 at 0,t,T, the unique time maximizing any detection has hazard coordinate clip((L+log[p1(1−πp3)/(p3(1−πp1))])/2,0,L), independent of p2, with exact endpoint regimes.
